business_problem: Siemens needed to bring AI, simulation, and digital-twin capabilities into industrial software products fast enough to offset labor shortages, shorten design cycles, and help manufacturing customers optimize complex assets without multiplying infrastructure cost.
solution_summary: Siemens is weaving NVIDIA technologies into multiple layers of its industrial software stack rather than treating AI as an add-on. Teamcenter uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to stream photorealistic, bill-of-materials-driven digital twins from centralized cloud GPU clusters, while Simcenter STAR-CCM+ uses CUDA acceleration to run massive CFD workloads natively on GPUs with CPU-consistent results. For knowledge work, the Siemens Industrial Copilot applies NIM and NeMo microservices to generate and explain operational guidance inside manufacturing workflows. On the physical-AI side, Siemens also uses Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Jetson Thor, and DGX systems to simulate, train, and deploy robotics and inspection scenarios before they reach the plant floor. Together these layers turn engineering data, simulation outputs, and shop-floor workflows into a reusable industrial AI platform.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Omniverse libraries
solution_components.role: Power Siemens digital-twin and visualization features inside Teamcenter and related industrial workflows.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA CUDA
solution_components.role: Accelerates Siemens simulation workloads such as CFD so engineering teams can solve larger models faster on GPU infrastructure.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA NIM
solution_components.role: Serves the inference layer behind copilots and AI services embedded in Siemens applications.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA NeMo
solution_components.role: Supports the enterprise AI microservices Siemens uses to customize and run industrial copilot capabilities.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
solution_components.role: Provides the simulation environment Siemens uses for robotics and physical-AI workflows before deployment.

data_flow: Engineering data and BOM-managed CAD assets flow into Teamcenter's Omniverse-backed digital twins, simulation workloads are processed through CUDA-accelerated solver paths, and enterprise process data is fed into NIM/NeMo-based copilots. For robotics scenarios, simulated assets and behaviors are validated in Isaac Sim before operators use them in live production settings.
business_outcome: Siemens reported 10 percent to 15 percent capital-expenditure reductions, a 25 percent reduction in reactive maintenance time, a 20 percent increase in throughput on initial digital-twin deployments, and early copilot pilots that improved productivity by about 30 percent with potential to reach 50 percent.
